fields.meta_description: Build a lessons learned survey template for release retros, construction closeouts, client projects, and a lessons log your PMO can filter.
fields.h1: Build a Lessons Learned Survey Template for Project Reviews
fields.hero_description: Build a lessons learned survey template your team answers at project close, with every lesson kept in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts in a Lessons Learned Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the lessons table behind it, and one prompt changes either before the next project closes.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your project

Describe the project and how it ended. Emergent drafts questions on what worked, what slowed the team down, and what to do again, and a follow-up prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Ratings for each project phase

Name the phases, such as design, procurement, and handover. Each gets one 1-5 rating and one open question, so a weak phase shows up as a number and the comments explain why.
fields.feature_3:
Candid answers, stored without names

The survey tracks who has replied so reminders stop, but stores each answer without a name. A project lead reads every comment and every score, never one person's set of answers.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders until the survey closes

Anyone who has not answered gets an email reminder 2 days before the close date, and the project lead gets a Slack list of who is still out. People who finished hear nothing more.
fields.feature_5:
Every lesson a row you can filter

Each answer lands as a row in a database you own, tagged with the project, the phase, and the close date. Filter by phase before a kickoff and read what the last 3 projects learned.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the lessons app.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a lessons learned survey template that my 12-person engineering team answers in Slack the day after a release ships.

faq_plan.q: What is a lessons learned survey template?
How do I create a lessons learned survey template?

plan.angle: The top 10 for lessons learned survey template are static Word, Excel and slide templates (Smartsheet, Asana, monday.com, Tempo, Conceptboard, Infotech, stakeholdermap) with what-went-well and what-went-wrong sections and no way to collect answers from a whole team or reuse them. This page shows four lessons learned surveys built from a prompt and run at project close: a software release retro answered in Slack, a construction closeout that rates each phase and emails the project manager about the weakest one, an agency project where the client and the team answer the same questions and disagree, and a lessons table a PMO filters before the next kickoff. The how-to gives the question design, timing and anonymity rules, and the FAQ covers question wording, timing, length, phase ratings and reuse.
tab_stories: Kessrow Software posts its lessons learned survey in the team's Slack channel the day after the 3.8 release ships, 11 of 12 engineers answer, 7 of 11 name the late QA environment as the biggest delay, and the team now books QA at sprint planning.

Ostgard Builders emails a closeout survey to 18 people on a clinic renovation, 15 answer, each of 5 phases is rated 1 to 5, procurement averages 2.1, and the project manager gets an email because it falls under the 2.5 threshold.

Arbelle Studio sends the same 6 questions to its 5-person team and 3 client stakeholders after a website relaunch, the team rates scope clarity 4.2 and the client rates it 2.3, a gap of 1.9 points, and the studio adds a one-page scope review to every proposal.

Rothmere Logistics' PMO tags every lesson by project and phase in one table, 3 closed projects produced 41 lessons, and before the next warehouse rollout the project lead filters the 6 tagged vendor onboarding into the kickoff agenda.
